issues.description: The solution's PersonResource constructor signature and implementation do not match the template and the intended design: in the solution the constructor takes a NoteService parameter and assigns this.personService = null, whereas the template (and correct DI wiring) expect a PersonService parameter that is stored in the personService field. This breaks dependency injection for PersonResource (personService remains null) and contradicts the template and problem description for implementing person endpoints, which will confuse students and prevent the server from functioning correctly.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution's PersonResource constructor to accept a PersonService parameter and assign it to the personService field (e.g. public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; }). Ensure the constructor signature matches the template so Spring can inject the correct service.

issues.description: The solution's PersonResource constructor declares a parameter of type NoteService and sets personService to null, whereas the problem statement and the template expect PersonResource to receive a PersonService. This renaming/type mismatch replaces the intended PersonService dependency with NoteService and leaves personService uninitialized, breaking the clear mapping between the described endpoints and the server-side dependency. Students reading the problem statement (which describes implementing PersonResource and forwarding actions to PersonService) and the template (which provides a constructor taking PersonService) will be confused by the solution's constructor signature and assignment.
issues.suggestedFix: Adjust the PersonResource constructor to accept PersonService and assign it to the field. For example: public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; } Ensure the parameter type and name match the field and the problem specification so the dependency injection and endpoint forwarding work as intended.
